title: Board of Governors closed for New Year's Day (observed) while the NYSE, the OCC and the Reserve Banks stay open — a full trading session, a quarterly expiration, and no Fed publishing desk
source: EST: federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/k8.htm, 'K.8 - Holidays Observed by the Federal Reserve System 2026-2030', fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 82,205 bytes, stamp 'Last Update: July 8, 2026') by the fomc-minutes-2027-12-29 initial-research adjacency sweep. The page states the split rule verbatim in its own header -- 'For holidays falling on Saturday, Federal Reserve Banks and Branches will be open the preceding Friday; however, the Board of Governors will be closed' -- and its footnote then names this exact date without inference: 'Saturday - the Federal Reserve Banks are open, but the Board of Governors is closed on July 3, 2026, June 18, 2027, December 24, 2027, December 31, 2027, and November 10, 2028.' The same page carries a dated correction confirming the Board revisited this specific observance: 'On July 8, 2026, the first footnote was updated to reflect the observance date for New Year's Day from December 31, 2028, to December 31, 2027.' THE MARKET SIDE IS THE OPPOSITE AND IS ALSO PRIMARY-SOURCED. nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200 after its 302, 109,180 bytes), gives no 2028 New Year's row at all and states why verbatim: 'Because the holiday falls on Saturday, January 1, 2028, no New Year's Day holiday is observed.' So 2027-12-31 is a FULL NYSE session. optionseducation.org/api/expirationcalendar (HTTP 200, 34,871 bytes) independently agrees on both counts: it carries no holiday flag on 2027-12-31 and marks the date a 'Quarterly Expiration date'. Filed estimate on this lane's standing no-self-confirm limit for an event discovered in-sweep, and because this calendar's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for an agency's own internal holiday schedule as distinct from a market calendar. THE DATE IS NOT IN DOUBT -- three independent primaries agree; the estimate label is about the taxonomy. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the fomc-minutes-2027-12-29 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-08), at D+2 from that release. LOAD-BEARING: this is the exact closure the proposer's date rule is measured against. That lane re-derived the FOMC minutes release census from the Board's own calendars (157 releases, 143 at exactly D+21) and found that December-class displacement is fully explained by distance from the BOARD's year-end closure rather than by the Christmas-New Year window -- |gap| <= 1 runs 4 displaced of 5, |gap| >= 2 runs 0 of 14 -- and 2027-12-29 sits at gap -2 from THIS date. Without this row the whole mechanism is unauditable from the calendar. IT IS ALSO WORTH A ROW ON ITS OWN TERMS, and the reason is the divergence, not the closure. Every other Fed-Board closure this calendar would ever carry coincides with a market closure and is therefore already covered by a *-market-closure-* entry (2027's other two Saturday cases, June 18 and December 24, are exactly juneteenth-market-closure-2027-06-18 and christmas-market-closure-2027-12-24). 2027-12-31 is the one 2027 date where they come apart: equities and options trade a full session, the OCC runs a quarterly expiration, the Reserve Banks are open for payments, and the agency that publishes FOMC minutes, the Beige Book, H.4.1 and every Board statistical release is shut. A calendar that tracks Fed communication needs to know that no Board publication can land that day. NOTHING TRADEABLE IS CLAIMED. symbols is empty, no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is calendar- or expiration-keyed, and the proposer measured the surrounding week and found it quieter than normal rather than exploitable (Dec 26-31 sessions 2007-2026: mean |S&P| 0.562% against a 0.798% universe). Proposed as an estimate; estimate widens caution and licenses no entry.
